description: General purpose library containing, in its current form, a very small collection of helpful functionalties that don't warrent a seperate library for each at this early stage.
releaseNotes:
10.3.3

Fixes in TextExtensions.Fill and FillDate, which Com.H.Text.Template's rendering also uses:

* Fixed: a value was read again after it was written. A placeholder inside a value was filled too,
  and removing a placeholder could join the text around it into a new one. Each placeholder is now
  replaced once, in the text as written, and the text of a value stays as it is.
* Fixed: with several QueryParams sets, a set that doesn't have a name wrote its NullReplacement
  before an earlier set could fill it, so in a template, a placeholder from the data model used
  inside a data tag's rows became "null". Of the sets whose markers find a placeholder, the latest
  one that has its name now fills it (with its NullReplacement when the value is null); when none
  of them has it, it gets the NullReplacement of the latest of them.
* Fixed: placeholders are now matched character by character, whatever the culture, and names are
  still looked up ignoring case. The culture-aware comparison used before could give a placeholder
  another one's value, for example one that differs only by a soft hyphen. With QueryParams sets,
  a marker written in another case is no longer filled either: {J{a}} for the marker {j{ used to be
  filled whenever {j{a}} also appeared.
* Fixed: markers are now matched as written. With markers that contain regex characters, such as
  [[ ]], (( )) or || ||, Fill with QueryParams sets found nothing, and Fill with a data model wrote
  nullValueReplacement into the wrong places, such as between every character.
* Fixed: a $ in a replacement was read as a regex substitution, so $0 wrote the placeholder back
  and $$ became $: in nullValueReplacement on every target, and with QueryParams sets on
  netstandard2.0 (and so .NET Framework), in a value or a NullReplacement.
* Fixed: Fill given a list of QueryParams as an object dropped each set's DataModel when neither
  markers nor a null replacement were given, so every placeholder got its NullReplacement, and
  ignored the markers and the null replacement when they were given.
* Fixed: Fill with a data model threw InvalidCastException for a value that isn't IConvertible,
  such as a Guid, DateTimeOffset or TimeSpan. Such a value is now written with its own formatting,
  in the invariant culture like that overload's other values.
* Fixed: two names that differ only in case got the same value. In FillDate, {date{mm}} took the
  month of {date{MM}}; in Fill with a data model that has both keys, both placeholders took the
  value of the key listed first. Each now takes the value for its own spelling.
* Fixed: Fill with a data model but without both markers applied nullValueReplacement to the whole
  text. With no marker it was written between every character, with only an opening marker it
  replaced every one left over, and with only a closing marker it replaced the text before each
  one left over. Without both markers, text with no value now stays as it is.

Upgrading from an earlier version? A value that holds a placeholder is no longer filled by a later
pass: fill that value first and pass the result. 10.3.1 changed what IOExtensions.UnifyPathSeperator
does with a leading // or \\ on Windows, and 10.3.0 changed how Com.H.Shell and Com.H.Pdf behave.
The notes of 10.3.0, 10.3.1 and 10.3.2 list every change:
https://www.nuget.org/packages/Com.H/10.3.2#releasenotes-body-tab
https://www.nuget.org/packages/Com.H/10.3.1#releasenotes-body-tab
https://www.nuget.org/packages/Com.H/10.3.0#releasenotes-body-tab
